atAGlance: Heo quay is roast pork with crisp skin, rich meat, and a salty-sweet fish-sauce dip. The crackling is the reason people order it.
whatItIs: Heo quay is roast pork with crackling skin and rich meat, usually eaten with rice, herbs, pickles, or sweet-sour fish-sauce dip.
howToEnjoy: Look for crisp skin and balance it with rice or pickles. If the skin matters to you, ask for skin-on pieces.
howLocalsOrder: Heo quay is ordered for crackly roasted pork skin, so ask for skin-on pieces if that is what you want. It is often eaten with rice, bánh hỏi, or pickles to cut the richness.
worthKnowing: Heo quay is common in rice plates, noodle pairings, and shared meals, but the crackling is the reason people seek it out. Good shops protect that brittle skin texture.
goodToKnow: Ask for skin-on pieces if you want the classic texture. Pickles, herbs, or rice cut through the richness.
travelerCaution: Contains pork and may include fatty skin-on pieces.
